title: Pythagoras’ Theorem (KS4)
subject: Maths
strapline: The rule linking the three sides of a right-angled triangle.
facts: Pythagoras’ theorem applies only to right-angled triangles.
It states a² + b² = c², where c is the hypotenuse (the longest side, opposite the right angle).
To find the hypotenuse: square the two shorter sides, add them, then square-root the total.
To find a shorter side: square the hypotenuse, subtract the other shorter side squared, then square-root.
Example: legs 3 and 4 give 9 + 16 = 25, so the hypotenuse is √25 = 5.
The hypotenuse is always the biggest number in the equation, so subtract when finding a shorter side.
It is used to find distances, including between two points on a coordinate grid.

quick_quiz.a: the longest side, opposite the right angle

quick_quiz.q: What is the formula for Pythagoras’ theorem?

teacher_tips: Get students to identify the hypotenuse before substituting anything.
Watch for the "subtract to find a shorter side" case — a frequent error.
Link to distance on a coordinate grid to show its real use.
